groups.text: It is currently a clear morning in Berlin-Tempelhof with a temperature of 21 degrees.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Chinese state-backed hacking groups have more than doubled their cyberattacks since they began using artificial intelligence for malware development and routine tasks. According to Taiwanese security firm TeamT5, hackers are utilizing models like DeepSeek because it is powerful and has very low cyber guardrails. Specifically, the group Grimfengxi used DeepSeek to write exploit code, while Teleboyi used the platform to map domains and collect IP addresses. Other tools have also appeared in these operations; a group called Slime22 used Anthropic's Claude Code to move through a Taiwanese company's systems, and security firm CyCraft found evidence of ChatGPT being used to build a decryption module for a Signal database. While a UK AI Safety Institute study notes that open models have seen a sharp jump in cyber capabilities, they still trail Western frontier models like Claude Mythos by several months regarding fully autonomous attacks.

Ukraine continues to face critical manpower shortages after more than four years of full-scale war. This shortage has sparked a growing debate over how the country can replenish its military ranks. Former Defense Minister Oleksii Reznikov recently suggested that Ukraine should consider making military service an obligation for all citizens, regardless of gender, citing Israel as a successful example of such a system. Former U.S. Special Envoy for Ukraine Keith Kellogg also supports mobilizing Ukrainian women into the military. In a recent interview, Kellogg stated that women fight no worse than men and argued it is very important for them to serve as part of society. He noted he sees no problem with this expansion personally or professionally, pointing to his own family's history where his daughter served in Afghanistan and his wife served as a paratrooper in Grenada.

Taiwanese prosecutors have charged nine people for illegally exporting high-end AI servers to mainland China. The group includes one employee from Nvidia and two from Super Micro. These servers used B300 graphics processing units, which are banned for sale to China under strict export controls. This crackdown follows years of tightening U.S. restrictions on advanced semiconductors, a key point of competition between Washington and Beijing. In France, the mutuelle Solimut is dealing with a different kind of security breach. The insurer alerted its 535,000 members to a cyberattack that occurred on Sunday, August 23. A hacker using the pseudonym ZeroBytes claims to have stolen data from 1.2 million insured people, including 770,000 bank accounts and over one million pay slips. Meanwhile, in India, researchers at the Mahuadanr Wolf Sanctuary are studying a more physical conflict. A new study identifies when wolves are most likely to attack livestock belonging to local tribal communities.

Turkish gas shipowner PascoGas has been linked to a new 370 million dollar deal with HD Hyundai for four LPG carriers. HD Hyundai Heavy Industries disclosed the order on Monday, though it identified the customer only as an Oceania-based shipping company. These ships are scheduled for delivery by March 31, 2030. This contract brings HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering’s 2026 order intake to 162 ships worth about 18 billion dollars, reaching over 77 percent of its full-year target. In a separate scientific effort, researchers have used samples from São Paulo and 101 other cities across 31 countries to catalog nearly 55 thousand species of RNA viruses. Published in Nature Communications, the study created the UPVAtlas by analyzing materials from hospitals, transport stations, and sewage. Roughly 77 percent of these viral species were previously unknown to science, though researchers note this does not necessarily mean new health threats have emerged.

The UK Competition and Markets Authority has accepted undertakings in lieu of reference regarding the acquisition of ChampionX Corporation by Schlumberger Limited. This decision follows a merger inquiry that began in November 2024 to evaluate the impact on the energy market sector. The regulator spent several months reviewing the deal, including a Phase 1 decision announced in January 2025 and a subsequent consultation period over the summer of 2025. By accepting these undertakings, the CMA avoided moving the case into a more intensive phase two investigation. To ensure the companies adhere to the agreed terms, the authority appointed a monitoring trustee on August 25, 2026. This move marks the final stage of a regulatory process designed to maintain competition while allowing the merger to proceed under specific conditions.

Major AI models are producing racist stereotypes based on ethnicity and nationality, according to tests conducted by Next. The findings began after comedian Alicia C’est Tout shared a viral video showing Google's AI summaries reacting differently to different nationalities; while a prompt about being alone with an Italian suggested enjoying the charm, a similar prompt regarding an Algerian triggered a warning to call the police. Further testing on Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude revealed that all three models show varying degrees of bias, favoring Western nationalities over others. In other news, fact-checkers at Dubawa have debunked claims circulating on X regarding Senegal's Minister of Economy, Finance, and Planning, Cheikh Diba. A post from user Mansour Dasylva alleged that the minister failed to declare his assets to the National Office for the Fight against Corruption. However, records confirm that Cheikh Diba did complete his declaration and is listed under the government section of the office's registry.

Chinese chemicals and energy group Jiahua Energy is expanding its logistics footprint by moving into shipowning. The company has ordered a 35,000 cubic meter carrier from CIMC Sinopacific Offshore & Engineering to reduce raw-material costs and increase throughput at its terminals. Total investment for the vessel and pre-operating costs is capped at 750 million yuan, or roughly 111 million dollars. Funding comes from Jiahua subsidiary Meifu Port & Storage and three partners through a new entity called Jiamei Shipping. Once delivered by late 2029, the ship will primarily serve coastal trades in Zhejiang and other Chinese regions under long-term contracts. In a different vein, physician Caroline Cherston has written an essay for STAT News reflecting on the parallels between whale songs and human expressions of love and loss. Drawing on her experience as an OB-GYN, she describes developing a trained ear for these sounds, specifically those sung by women.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be mostly clear with temperatures between 21 and 24 degrees and rain chances up to 8 percent.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.

On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has Antje's birthday, and a visit to Krebs at six in the evening. Your work calendar has NAS Sync at two in the afternoon, followed by the RAYX Meeting at three.
Mail worth checking: The Anthropic Team sent you six free months of Claude Max. Also, Discord confirmed your account deletion request was processed.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
